lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: risk return and time horizon

objective: Learners compute invented compound growth at two rates over the same horizon and quantify how much the rate difference is worth.
scenario: Anika is an invented seventh grader modelling $1,000.00 over three simulated years at two invented rates: 5% a year and 2% a year, each compounding annually. All figures are invented for practice.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Grow Anika's invented $1,000.00 at 5% a year for three years, compounding each year on the new balance.

prompts.text: What is the balance after three years at 5%?

tasks.directions: Run the same three years at Anika's lower invented rate of 2%, then compare the two ending balances.

prompts.text: What is the balance after three years at 2%?
How much more does the 5% rate produce over three years?

tasks.directions: Compare the compounded result at 5% with what simple interest at the same rate would have produced over three years.

prompts.text: What would three years of simple interest at 5% produce as a balance?
How much does compounding add over simple interest in three years?

tasks.directions: Three years made compounding worth less than eight dollars.

prompts.text: Compounding added little over three years in Anika's model. Explain what changes over a much longer horizon and why time matters more than the first few years suggest.

remediation: If a learner multiplies the first year's interest by three, write out each of Anika's three years in sequence with its own opening balance.
extension: Ask the learner to project Anika's 5% balance for a fourth and fifth year and describe how the yearly increase changes.
